name: The Epiphany of the Lord
history: Epiphany means showing forth. The Church celebrates Christ revealed to the nations in the Magi, wise men from the East who followed a star to Bethlehem and offered gold, frankincense and myrrh. The ancient liturgy joins to this day two other manifestations: His baptism in the Jordan and the first sign at the wedding at Cana. In some countries the feast is kept on the nearest Sunday.
life: Saint Matthew alone tells of the Magi. He does not say they were kings or that there were three; tradition drew the number from their three gifts and, from the Psalms, came to call them kings. Gold was offered to a king, frankincense to God and myrrh to one who would die. The Fathers saw in their journey the call of the Gentiles, all the peoples outside Israel, into the one family of God. In the East the feast is older than Christmas. On this day the Church traditionally announces the date of Easter for the coming year, water is blessed, and households chalk their doors with the year and the letters C, M and B, for Caspar, Melchior and Balthasar and for Christus mansionem benedicat, may Christ bless this house. In London the Chapel Royal still offers gold, frankincense and myrrh in the sovereign’s name.
prayerTo: Lord Jesus, you led the Magi by a star to find you with Mary your mother. Lead me also, through the darkness of this world, to kneel before you. Take the gold of my love, the incense of my prayer and the myrrh of my sorrows, and let me go home, like them, by another way. Amen.
penance: Chalk the lintel of your door with the year and the letters C, M and B, and pray for all who live there and all who visit. Give a gift to the poor in place of one to yourself.
meditation: They went home by another road. Now that you have met Christ, what in your life should take a different road?
prayer: O God, You Who by the guidance of a star this day revealed Your only-begotten Son to the Gentiles; mercifully grant that we who know You now by faith, may come to behold You in glory. Through the same Christ our Lord…
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
